clauses.reason: The sentence exempts Bernice Pyke from compulsory retirement for age, effective as of April 1, 1950, “for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires”. The cap is the order's own end and equals the date her present term expires, so it is recorded as the end, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when March 31, 1952 begins. Executive Order 10333 of March 25, 1952 further exempts her for a new indefinite period “not extending beyond the appointment and qualification of her successor”; that is a later extension with its own term and is not treated as an end of this order.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10225 (16 FR 2544 (Federal Register of March 20, 1951)) was signed March 17, 1951. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only operative command exempts Bernice Pyke, Collector of Customs for Customs Collection District No. 41 with headquarters at Cleveland, Ohio, from compulsory retirement for age under the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, effective as of April 1, 1950 (the order was signed nearly a year after that date), “for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated by its own terms on March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires. Executive Order 10333 (17 FR 2705 (Federal Register of March 28, 1952)), signed March 25, 1952, recites this order, says that she was exempted by it for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, and further exempts her for an indefinite period “not extending beyond the appointment and qualification of her successor”. That is a later extension by a new order with its own term, recorded as a later event and not as the end of this order; it also shows that the exemption had not lapsed before March 25, 1952. The person-name search found Executive Order 10333 and the neighbouring Federal Register page that also prints this order (Executive Order 10224 on the same page); no other held text names her. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order.

savings.reason: The exemption only allows continued service despite reaching retirement age; the order creates no right that outlives March 31, 1952, has no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no instrument continuing this exemption other than the separate further exemption in Executive Order 10333.
